sentences.text: Oli Coppock had a career in digital marketing and was feeling positive about his future In May 2024, a few months after having treatment for a brain tumour, Oli Coppock went to Warrington Hospital's emergency department with bad headaches and dizziness.

sentences.text: He underwent tests and assessments, but did not have a brain scan, before going home.

sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.text: Despite the brain tumour and a recent diagnosis of multiple sclerosis, Oli was otherwise fit and well and positive about his future.
sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.text: Stephen Coppock says the whole family has been left broken by what happened to Oli "The hospital didn't get the basics right and my son has paid a terrible price – it's ruined his life.
sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.text: He trusted the health service and believed it was there to help him, not destroy him." He says Oli's body is now twisted and paralysed and he has no ability to move around.
sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.text: His breathing, feeding and toileting are all done through tubes at the neurological rehabilitation centre where he is being cared for.
sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.text: In a statement, the trust said: "We are deeply sorry that Mr Coppock did not receive that standard of care that should be expected and we recognise the distress and lasting impact on patients and their families when harm is caused." An interim damages payment has been agreed.
sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.text: However, Oli's solicitor, Tanzeela Aslam, head of medical negligence at Express Solicitors, says the time taken to get to this point – more than two years – has just added to the failings, depriving him of access to funds for therapies and support that could have improved his quality of life.
sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.text: "Oli's case illustrates how preventable errors within the NHS can have devastating and life-changing consequences for individuals and their families." She says she is seeing more and more A&E-related cases – something she too puts down to the growing pressures.
sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.text: It means A&E is now the single biggest area for clinical negligence claims in terms of number.
sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.text: The pattern is not being repeated in other areas, such as maternity or orthopaedics, and the low point in 2020-21 is thought to be unrelated to any behaviour changes by patients during the Covid pandemic as it takes three years on average for a claim to be submitted.

sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.text: But it is not surprising when you see how busy departments are.

sentences.text: People are staying longer and pressure on staffing is increasing." But he said clinical negligence cases were still relatively rare – happening in only around one in every 17,000 attendances.

sentences.text: Such mistakes include missing the signs of acute deterioration in patients, failing to order the necessary tests and scans and making incorrect diagnoses.
sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.article_title: A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32

sentences.text: Trump's territorial ambitions have repeatedly strained relations with neighbouring countries Iceland has summoned the US ambassador after President Donald Trump posted a map on social media that appeared to show Iceland and several other countries covered by the American flag.

sentences.text: Trump posted the image on Truth Social on Monday, showing the US, Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean covered in stars and stripes.

sentences.text: The entire landmass was labelled "United States of America".

sentences.text: Iceland's foreign minister said the post was "completely inappropriate".

sentences.text: Trump's territorial ambitions have repeatedly strained relations with neighbouring countries, including his push to acquire Greenland and calls to make Canada the America's 51st state.
sentences.article_title: Iceland summons US ambassador over Trump's stars and stripes map

sentences.text: His post of the map did not include a caption and preceded a  flurry of posts of maps renaming the US state of New Mexico as "New America".
sentences.article_title: Iceland summons US ambassador over Trump's stars and stripes map

sentences.text: Responding to Trump's post, Iceland's Foreign Minister Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir called in US ambassador to Iceland Billy Long, who formally took up the post last month, local media reported.

sentences.text: Kent Police says it was warned about possible protests in Dover the day before they took place, but information "was not fully assessed" Kent Police has said it was made aware of the potential for protests in Dover the day before they took place but information "was not fully assessed".
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: A large group of protesters dressed in black and wearing balaclavas blocked access to the Port of Dover on Saturday for several hours, with witnesses hearing chants of "stop the boats".
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: Kent Police had said it did not know about the demonstration in advance , leading to accusations of a failure in intelligence-gathering.
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: But the force said a review had found it received non-emergency information late on Friday which may have allowed it to "consider its resourcing", but did not share what it was told.
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: The Home Office has declined to comment.
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: A force spokesperson said: "The protest organisers adopted a different approach to previous protests, and as part of our commitment to public safety we have examined our decision-making to identify any lessons, to ensure we are well prepared for future events organised in a similar way.
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: "During that initial review, we found the force had received non-emergency information late on Friday evening that a protest could take place in the town the following day.
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: "This information was not fully assessed.
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: If it was, it may have allowed the force to consider its resourcing." Protesters blocked the port from 07:00 BST for several hours on Saturday Kent Police previously said the protest was "spontaneous", and it did not have any intelligence to suggest a demonstration was going to happen.
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: Dover District Council deputy keader Edward Biggs called the announcement from Kent Police "very worrying" and "really poor".
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: He added: "It's very disappointing.
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: We rely on the police providing us information so that we can inform the community and take whatever steps we need to take." Kent Police said the information it received "would not have prevented the lawful protest from taking place, nor the disruption experienced by the town, port and wider community".
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: It said it had asked the College of Policing to independently examine the processes involved, so it can learn from its response.
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: Kent's police and crime commissioner Matthew Scott said he welcomed the independent learning review by the College of Policing.
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: He said he had asked that it examined both how information is triaged and the communications strategy the force deployed in response to the event.
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: He said he would ensure the chief constable was held to account with regards to any recommendations made.
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: He added: "It is essential that we understand how this happened, and that lessons are learnt.
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: No arrests were made on the day of the protest, police said previously.
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: Although no boats arrived on Saturday, eight did on Sunday, carrying 625 people, Home Office figures revealed.
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: The day after the protest, several officers were injured and vehicles damaged in Portsmouth at a demonstration sparked by the arrival of 120 migrants.
sentences.article_title: Police warned a day before Dover protest, force says

sentences.text: Both protests have been linked to Danny Thomas , a long-term campaigner against migrants more commonly known as Danny Tommo.

sentences.text: Barnaby Webber, Grace O'Malley-Kumar and Ian Coates were stabbed to death by Valdo Calocane on 13 June 2023 The death of a student killed in the Nottingham attacks was "potentially preventable", a public inquiry has heard.

sentences.text: Alan MacPherson amassed a collection of more than two million child abuse images A pensioner who amassed what is thought to be the largest collection of child sexual abuse material ever seized by police in Scotland has been jailed for four years.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: Alan MacPherson, 83, from Stenhousemuir, was found to have more than two million images on various electronic devices after his home was raided in 2025.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: More than 805,000 were identified as depicting child sexual abuse - much of it in the most serious category - while the overwhelming scale of his collection meant much of material was not checked and categorised.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: MacPherson was told by Sheriff Mayram Labaki that the scale of his crime was "exceptional".
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: The sheriff said: "The quantity [of images] was so great that a substantial proportion could not be examined and categorised by forensic examiners.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: "Every image records the abuse or exploitation of a child.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: The possession and circulation of such material perpetuates that abuse." MacPherson will also be supervised for three years following his release from jail and placed on the sex offenders register for life.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: The former volunteer archivist with the Royal Scottish Country Dance Society previously admitted downloading the material over a 14-year period.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: Sheriff Labaki added: "Your views towards your offending and your victims are unconscionable.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: "I refer specifically to the passages in the [social work] report where you state that not only were the children consenting, but they were willing participants.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: "Your attitude is unremorseful".
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: Falkirk Sheriff Court was told that police seized nine devices – computers, phones, digital cameras, a USB stick and external drives – and child abuse material was found on all of them.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: Five of the devices were subjected to a full examination.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: The court heard previously that almost 1.4 million images remained ungraded on one of the devices, due to the extent of the collection.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: MacPherson was caught after police identified his IP address was being used to distribute child abuse material.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: Prosecutor Rachel Wallace said that in July 2025, MacPherson posted multiple images of child sexual exploitation, classed as the most serious, during an online chat with an undercover police officer.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: Although he was using a messaging app designed to be anonymous, police were able to trace the messages to his home.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: The child victims were girls, mostly aged between nine and 15, but at least one was possibly as young as seven.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: Wallace said: "Police have advised us this is quite possibly the largest collection of child sexual abuse material ever seen by Police Scotland." When MacPherson was arrested and interviewed, he told police he had searched online for years for indecent images of children "for his own personal gratification".
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: Solicitor advocate Stephen Biggam, defending, said MacPherson would "steadily lose his eyesight" due to macular degeneration.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: He said: "The court might take the view that will eliminate or significantly mitigate any risk going forward.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: "His wife has served divorce papers on him in custody.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: "It's been made plain to him that his wife, his son, and 99% of people in general, want nothing more to do with him." MacPherson was a prominent figure in The Royal Scottish Country Dance Society and in 2003 he was photographed with Queen Elizabeth II - its patron - at Holyrood Palace.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the society said: "We are shocked and appalled by the offences committed by Alan MacPherson and the details which have emerged through these court proceedings.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: "The society takes the safeguarding and wellbeing of everyone involved in its activities extremely seriously and has clear safeguarding policies and procedures in place." He said the society was not aware of any concerns being raised previously in relation to MacPherson.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: "However, given his longstanding involvement in Scottish country dancing, the organisation will now undertake a full and thorough review of his involvement with the society.

sentences.text: "As well as this investigation into Mr MacPherson, the board will also review all of our existing policies." He said anyone with concerns relating to MacPherson or his involvement in the society should contact them.
sentences.article_title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed

sentences.text: Anthony Hall (left) had admitted all four charges at a hearing on 31 July A blind motorist who took his partner's car and drove for 150 miles (240km) at night while drunk has been handed a suspended sentence.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: Anthony Hall, 50, who does not have a driving licence, was stopped by police on the M6 near Carlisle at 01:45 BST on 29 June after he was seen swerving the Vauxhall Meriva between lanes and onto the hard shoulder, a court was told.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: Hall told police he had driven from his home in Huddersfield after he and his partner had drunk four bottles of wine.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: Kirklees Magistrates' Court heard Hall, of Lees Close, had admitted charges including dangerous driving at a previous hearing and was sentenced on Tuesday to 36 weeks in prison, suspended for 18 months.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: Hall had also admitted drink-driving, driving without a licence or insurance and taking a car without consent.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: The court heard that in the early hours of 29 June, police received information there was a driver on the M6 northbound who was under the influence and was blind.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: Hall was pulled over by a police officer after the Vauxhall was seen swerving near junction 42.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: The officer who stopped Hall could smell alcohol on his breath and, when asked about this, the 50-year-old said he and his partner had drunk wine.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: Hall told the officer he had gone blind about two years ago but could see some lights and he explained that while on the motorway he had followed an HGV's lights.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: The distance Hall had travelled was about 150 miles and he had taken the car from his partner without permission, according to police.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: Kirklees Magistrates' Court heard Hall had no previous convictions When he was breathalysed at the side of the road, Hall gave a reading of 50 micrograms of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: At a police station later, he gave a reading of 46 micrograms of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: The drink-drive limit in England and Wales is 35 micrograms of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: Hall told police he had planned to drive to Scotland and wanted to escape his home, his relationship and his finances.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: The court heard he had stopped for fuel at an unknown location where an attendant had filled up his car.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: No-one was injured during the incident.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: In mitigation, Adele Graham said her client had no previous convictions and he had suffered a breakdown before setting off on the journey.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: Hall had felt trapped in his own home and wanted to get as far away from his life there as possible, she said.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: "This was an individual in crisis making a poor decision while in crisis," she said.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: Sentencing Hall, magistrate Tracey McErlain-Burns said Hall was of previous good character and had some difficult personal circumstances.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: She explained that while the custody threshold had been crossed, she had decided to suspend any custodial sentence.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: Hall was sentenced to 36 weeks in prison, suspended for 18 months.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: Meanwhile, he was told he must carry out rehabilitation activities and abstain from alcohol for 90 days.
sentences.article_title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk

sentences.text: Demand for avocados in India has been booming Fifteen years ago there was almost no market for avocados in India, remembers Madhu Bopaiah.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: Ripe fruit would fall off trees and be eaten by dogs, earning avocados the unappetising name dog fruit, he says.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: Bopaiah has been working in India's plantation industry for 26 years, he's currently group manager at Cottanad Plantations, which grows cocoa, rubber, coffee, spices and fruits, including avocado, in the hills of Wayanad in the southern Indian state of Kerala.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: "We never planted avocado as our main crop.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: We introduced it as a shade tree for coffee plantations, and only later realised it could become a profitable business," he says.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: He says the turning point was around 2011 when Bollywood star Shilpa Shetty said she used avocado for skincare.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: "Overnight, prices doubled and then kept rising," he says.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: Cottanad has responded to that demand by planting avocado trees on 40 acres.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: Last year they harvested between 10 and 15 tonnes of fruit.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: In three of four years time they hope to raise that to 40 to 50 tonnes.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: There's been a lot to learn.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: "We completely changed the way we grow avocados after learning from South African experts.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: Today we use raised beds, wider spacing and different planting methods because avocado roots are highly vulnerable to diseases," Bopaiah says.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: There's plenty of scope for Indian farmers to step-up production.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: "When we studied the market, we found a huge gap between demand and supply.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: India imports around 15,000 tonnes of avocados every year, while domestic production is only about 8,000–9,000 tonnes," says Manilal Palliyath who helps promote India's avocado industry.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: He sees a big opportunity for farmers, particularly as traditional crops have suffered.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: "Coffee and pepper have suffered because of changing climatic conditions, making diversification essential for farmers." Indian restaurants are offering more avocado dishes While demand is growing in India, it's not always for locally grown fruit.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: "Indian-grown avocados are improving and there are some great farmers working with local varieties, but the quality and availability can vary significantly depending on the season and region," says Hussain Shahzad, the executive chef at Hunger Inc.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: The group owns four restaurants in Mumbai, including Veronica's and The Bombay Canteen.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: "We have explored different varieties of avocados available in India, but the imported ones currently offer the consistency we need in terms of flavour, texture, size, and ripening," he says But like many in the catering industry, he would like to source ingredients locally.

sentences.text: "We are always interested in exploring better local produce as it evolves.

sentences.text: Harshit Godha is the founder of Indo-Israel Avocado Nursery in Bhopal, in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: He founded the nursery business in 2021, after spending a month in Israel learning about the industry.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: Since then, business has been brisk.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: Over the last five years Godha has supplied around 18,000 avocado plants to farmers across India.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: All of the saplings are international varieties like Hass and Pinkerton.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: "Israel grows avocados on approximately 13,000 hectares - a small country with almost no rainfall for eight months of the year.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: This is precisely why Israeli avocado technology is the most advanced in the world," Godha says.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: Getting a commercial orchard up and running is not easy.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: It is a very different operation from the traditional way of cultivating avocados in India, where they were planted among other crops for shade.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: For a start, you can't just grow a tree from seed.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: A commercial tree comprises a rootstock, chosen for its tolerance to local conditions, grafted to the upper half which determines what sort of fruit is produced.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: Once that's done the trees need a lot of attention.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: "When you put in a professional orchard, you have to know the techniques of pruning.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: A tree can grow up to 25 feet within six to seven years, and harvesting at 25 feet is next to impossible," Godha says.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: "Aggressive" pruning is needed to keep the harvest at a height that's convenient for workers.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: On top of that an avocado tree cannot easily pollinate itself.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: To get fruit two different varieties of avocado trees have to be planted right next to each other.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: One variety needs to be open as a female at the exact same time the other variety is releasing pollen as a male." "If a farmer gets this planting ratio wrong, the trees will fail to produce fruit, no matter how advanced the irrigation tech is.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: This single botanical detail is what separates a highly profitable, high-yielding orchard from one that looks great on paper but fails in reality," says Godha.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: The Arka Supreme is a domestically developed avocado variety Using popular foreign varieties is one way of modernising India's avocado industry.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: Another is improving trees that have in India for generations.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: "The biggest issue with the avocado trees in India are that every backyard tree is genetically different," says Dr Ganeshan Karunakaran, the principal scientist at the ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: "That is why Indian markets are flooded with mixed fruit of varying quality.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: Standard varieties are essential if we want a reliable commercial market." For 25 years he has been working on a breeding project which has released two varieties, based on local trees.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: "Our objective is to provide farmers with uniform, high-yielding, good-quality planting material rather than thousands of different unnamed trees," Karunakaran says.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: He is also concerned about unregulated nurseries selling unidentified, or diseased plants.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: "Farmers may unknowingly buy diseased plants.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: The trees may look healthy initially, but after five or seven years they can suddenly die, causing huge financial losses," he says.
sentences.article_title: From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom

sentences.text: Despite the challenges, farmers see the potential in switching to avocado cultivation.

sentences.text: Eight years ago he dedicated two acres of his farm in Wayanad Kerala, to the crop.

sentences.text: "Avocado will never fail you.

sentences.text: It's such a loving and lovable fruit.

sentences.text: I have fallen in love with this fruit now.

sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "It's been two years since my diagnosis and I've felt that I've started to understand the disease a lot better and the way it affects my life.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "I'm going to have to spend the rest of my life being treated for this," she added.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: Moshiri was diagnosed in November 2024 with polycythaemia vera (PV) - a rare, treatable blood cancer.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: Although it cannot be cured, it can be managed effectively.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: In PV, your body makes too many red blood cells, which makes the blood thicker than normal.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: It leads to a higher risk of developing blood clots, which can cause a stroke, heart attack or deep vein thrombosis (DVT).
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: Symptoms can include headaches, confusion, dizziness and blurred vision.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "I was told by my consultant that I have this incurable blood cancer," she said.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "Mostly I had no symptoms and that's one of the problems with this disease.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "The only reason mine was caught was because my GP was so fastidious in the way she did my routine blood tests and immediately sent them for further diagnosis." As part of her initial treatment, the BBC News chief presenter underwent several "debilitating" hour-long sessions of venesections.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: Venesection is a procedure where a needle is put into a vein in the arm to slowly draw the blood out.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: This blood letting can be an effective way to reduce the thickness of the blood.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "In about a space of five months, I had venesection seven or eight times.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: So you can imagine my iron levels hit the floor and I felt even more exhausted," she said.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "After a while I started feeling extremely unwell and tired.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: I started losing my hair, I got itchy all over my body, but the main symptom was fatigue." Later, The World Today presenter was able to get on an immunotherapy treatment called interferon through the NHS, and after some tweaks, she says she is in a better place.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "I've only needed one venosection in about 15 months, so that's been really good.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: The last couple of months have been better than the last two years," she said.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "I think it's really important people understand that this blood cancer is incurable but it's manageable with the right treatment and you can lead a relatively healthy life.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "It's just a question of finding the right treatment and making sure it works for you." She admits she is "not the person I was two years ago" but says she feels "much better".
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: In a few cases, PV can develop into another type of blood cancer called myelofibrosis, and even more rarely can develop into a type of leukaemia called acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), according to charity Blood Cancer UK which funds research into blood cancers.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: Moshiri has continued to cover the biggest news stories while living with the cancer The mother-of-three said she has had to adjust to life with her condition, sometimes not being able to attend family occasions or play with her children because she is exhausted.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "It's the kind of fatigue that is not like I'm just tired and I didn't get a good night's sleep, you feel like someone has removed your battery completely, and however much sleep you get makes no difference," she explains.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "Even though I feel the best I have in two years, I don't know how I'm going to be in six months, one year, two years.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: She credits her "supportive and helpful" husband Jonathan, management at the BBC and her children Iris, 13, Vivienne, 11 and Caspian, 9.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "It took me a long time to be able to tell them about this illness, because I don't want to worry them, but they have been so understanding.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: When I say things like 'mummy is too tired to play with you', they get it and they don't push it," she said.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "There is a lot of research going into blood cancer and scientific advancement to look forward to.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: An at-home urine test that the NHS has been trialling can detect more than nine in ten cases of bladder cancer, latest findings show.

sentences.text: The study, published in European Urology Oncology, was led by the University of Birmingham and a diagnostics company Nonacus, and involved nearly 1,000 patients at seven hospitals in England and Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Urine test can spot more than nine in 10 bladder cancers

sentences.text: Researchers hope it could reduce the number of patients needing urgent, more invasive procedures, called cystoscopies, which involve inserting a small camera up the urethra and into the bladder.
sentences.article_title: Urine test can spot more than nine in 10 bladder cancers

sentences.text: If a larger trial is successful, it could mean tens of thousands of patients a year are spared these tests.
sentences.article_title: Urine test can spot more than nine in 10 bladder cancers

sentences.text: More than 300,000 cystoscopies are performed in the UK each year and there are significant waiting lists in some areas.
sentences.article_title: Urine test can spot more than nine in 10 bladder cancers

sentences.text: While the urine test is not a replacement for cystoscopies, it could help doctors identify patients at greater risk who should be prioritised for urgent ones rather than wait.
sentences.article_title: Urine test can spot more than nine in 10 bladder cancers

sentences.text: This NHS trial found that the Galeas urine test identified 92% of bladder cancer cases.
sentences.article_title: Urine test can spot more than nine in 10 bladder cancers

sentences.text: A negative result meant there was more than a 99% chance that the patient did not have bladder cancer.
sentences.article_title: Urine test can spot more than nine in 10 bladder cancers

sentences.text: It checks for any genetic material shed into the urine by bladder cancer and was originally developed by the University of Birmingham with funding from Cancer Research UK (CRUK).
sentences.article_title: Urine test can spot more than nine in 10 bladder cancers

sentences.text: It looks for more than 450 DNA mutations associated with bladder cancer across 23 genes.
sentences.article_title: Urine test can spot more than nine in 10 bladder cancers

sentences.text: Prof Richard Bryan, co-author of the study and from Birmingham University, said after spending years developing and evaluating the science, it was exciting to see "very promising early performance" in a large real-world patient population.
sentences.article_title: Urine test can spot more than nine in 10 bladder cancers

sentences.text: Under a licensing agreement, the test has been commercialised by Nonacus, which pays back part of the revenue to the University and CRUK.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Ella, who was diagnosed at 24, explains the symptoms of HSD Vivienne Duval has always been flexible.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: She can do every yoga pose there is, but it was not until she turned 58 that she realised that this bendiness was not a good thing.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: In fact, it was the answer to all of the strange health problems she had been experiencing for years - issues with digestion, fatigue, and pain.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: Earlier this year, when Vivienne came across a video on social media explaining the symptoms of Hypermobility Spectrum Disorder, it was like a light bulb switching on.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: "I saw myself in everything they were saying," she tells me.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: "So I armed myself with all the information and went to my doctor." Vivienne's hunch was confirmed - she had hypermobile joints.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: "I had all these separate things, but no one had ever put them all together.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: Now it's blindingly obvious." The disorder may affect hundreds of thousands of people in the UK, but many - like Vivienne - face significant delays in getting a diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: Vivienne Duval was diagnosed at the age of 58, after decades of wondering what was going on with her body Hypermobility Spectrum Disorders (HSD) are connective tissue disorders that cause joint hypermobility - when joints have a greater-than-normal range of motion.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: Due to lax collagen between connective tissues, muscles have to work harder to keep joints stable, leading to fatigue and pain, as well as clumsiness.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: HSD can also cause gastrointestinal symptoms because the connective tissue within the digestive system is stretchier.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: Links between HSD and neurodiversity such as autism and ADHD have also been established.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: Some people, like Vivienne, also have hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (hEDS), which is diagnosed by looking for hypermobility and faulty connective tissue throughout the body, as well as musculoskeletal issues like dislocations.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: Hypermobility disorders may affect hundreds of thousands of people in the UK, though many remain undiagnosed, according to new research , external from the University of Edinburgh.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: It found patients with hEDS and HSD in the UK waited an average of 19 to 21.7 years for diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: The diagnostic process for HSD is complicated by the fact the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence does not have a dedicated, standalone clinical guideline for diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: Dr Jessica Eccles, a researcher on brain-body interactions and hypermobility, says diagnosis can be a "postcode lottery in terms of where you are and what opportunities are available to you for assessment".
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: She adds that HSD and hEDS seem to affect women more.
sentences.article_title: Hypermobility - the little-known 'bendy disease' that causes pain and fatigue

sentences.text: Sleep scores, magnesium, white noise machines - what was once the simple act of sleeping has become a minefield.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Trying to optimise sleep in this way is called "sleepmaxxing".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Take it too far, and you could end up with "orthosomnia" - the clinical term for an obsession with achieving perfect sleep.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: While it's not formally recognised as a condition in the UK, doctors tell the BBC they've noticed signs of orthosomnia in their patients, with some bringing their sleep tracker data into appointments convinced, wrongly, that they have a sleep disorder.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: That fixation is actually making people's sleep worse, they warn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: So how and why did sleep become so complicated?
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: And if sleepmaxxing isn't the answer, what is the elusive secret to a good night's sleep?
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The first commercial fitness tracker to incorporate sleep analysis was the Fitbit Classic in 2009.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Since then, many others - including Garmin, Whoop and Apple - have integrated sleep trackers into wrist-worn devices, as have smart rings such as Oura, Ultrahuman and RingConn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: These devices vary, but in general they all provide users with a report of their night, broken down by sleep stages - time awake, light sleep, deep sleep, and REM (rapid eye movement).
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Many also give users a "sleep score".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: But the concept of a sleep score is "completely made up", according to Dr Alanna Hare, consultant of sleep medicine at the Royal Brompton Hospital in London.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "There's nothing recognised in sleep science that is a 'sleep score'," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "That's just been created by manufacturers." This video can not be played How sleep-tracking can make your sleep worse Hare says she's noticed trackers causing anxiety among her patients.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I've noticed more patients coming to me with data from various trackers, with lots of questions about sleep that... is probably contributing to their sleep difficulties," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Even though some have had medical tests with reassuring results, this hasn't allayed their fears, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "It's great that there's more focus on sleep as part of wellness," she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "But sleep just does not respond well to attempts to perfect it." One proposed lawsuit against Oura, filed last month in San Francisco, alleges that Oura rings are unable to accurately measure sleep quality and sleep stages, and instead rely on AI-generated estimates that have "a coin flip's chance of being correct".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: In response, Oura told the BBC that it "stand[s] behind our science, research and accuracy claims".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "We're committed to clearly communicating what Oura measures, what it estimates, and how members should use that information," the company added.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Studies also show sleep trackers can affect how you function during the day, even if they're not accurate.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: In one study , external from the University of Oxford, participants were given sleep trackers which assigned them a sleep score.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The scores were randomised, however, and had no relation to how the participants had actually slept.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The next day participants rated their mood, fatigue levels and alertness, before tests checking their focus and reaction times.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Researchers found that the people told they'd slept badly reported feeling more fatigued, and were less mentally alert - even though the sleep scores were all fake.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: This is something Jess Hill says she noticed in herself after getting a Garmin watch several years ago.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I started to rely on the watch as my Bible for whether I slept well or not," the 32-year-old HR professional from London tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I would think, 'I've had awful sleep so I'm going to really struggle today', even if I actually probably had okay sleep.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I was awake the other week for four hours in the night, and my watch was like 'wow, great sleep!' - I literally was awake from 01:00 until 05:00," she says.

sentences.text: The BBC has approached Garmin for comment.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Jess's sleep scores weren't matching how she actually felt Dr Neil Stanley, sleep expert and author of the book How to Sleep Well, argues that gamifying sleep is creating more disordered sleeping.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "The thing with tracking your sleep is that it gives you a number, and this means you have a target," he tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "So you get into this cycle of worrying about your quality of sleep or the quantity of sleep based on figures." He says he carried out research into actigraphy - wrist-worn sleep trackers - around 40 years ago.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Though commercial trackers now are a bit more sophisticated, they work in much the same way - by measuring your movement - and have the same limitations, he says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "If you want to measure sleep, you have to measure the brain," Stanley adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "Unless you're measuring the brain's activities, you're not measuring sleep." Keeping your bedroom cool, dark and quiet - within reason.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "That doesn't mean it needs to be pitch black, exactly 16C or totally silent," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "It should be coolish, darkish and quietish." Seeing bright light in the morning, which is good for regulating your circadian rhythm - that is, your body's natural clock.

sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The NHS Alliance, which represents health managers, says the current system in England represents a "bad deal" for patients and taxpayers alike.

sentences.article_title: NHS bosses warn of chaos in ADHD and autism care

sentences.article_title: NHS bosses warn of chaos in ADHD and autism care

sentences.text: Lucy Shepherd was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2019 A breast cancer survivor says she no longer lives "with the same fear" after a clinical trial enabled her to stop the heart medication she needed following cancer treatment.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Lucy Shepherd, from Hertfordshire, was diagnosed with triple positive breast cancer shortly after her 33rd birthday, but a routine scan revealed that her heart function had declined during care.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: A new study, described as "hugely encouraging" for patients, has found the majority of breast cancer survivors whose treatment caused heart problems may not need to be on precautionary medication for life.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: "Being part of the trial and having the chance to come off my heart medication has definitely improved my life," Shepherd said.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: The trial - funded by the British Heart Foundation - involved 90 women in their 40s and 50s across four UK hospitals, whose hearts had recovered after a specific type of treatment for breast cancer.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Most would have been advised to stay on heart drugs for life over concerns heart function would decline if they stopped.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Researchers found that 98% of patients in the group who stopped taking medication had no change in heart function after one year, with just one woman developing a problem with her heart's pumping ability.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Women who came off drugs also reported, in questionnaires, a better quality of life.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Shepherd developed heart problems related to her cancer treatment Shepherd, now 39, said: "Living beyond my cancer treatment was difficult because no one could tell me whether I should stop or continue taking my heart medication.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: "As I got fitter after my cancer treatment ended doctors gradually reduced my heart medication dosages, but I was still having side effects like a low heart rate and fatigue.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: I also had the mental burden of remembering to take them and the worry of what would happen if I missed a dose.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: "I'm still taking hormone therapy, but I don't live with the same fear I once had.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: "Modern breast cancer treatment is a remarkable success story," she said.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: "But the damaging effects of these drugs on the heart leaves survivors and their doctors with difficult questions about ongoing treatment to maintain their heart health.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: "Our study provides the first evidence that heart failure therapies can be safely stopped in survivors whose hearts have recovered, with the support of ongoing close monitoring.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: But the researchers suggest their findings can start important conversations between survivors and their doctors about whether they need to continue treatment long-term.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Breast cancer is the most common cancer in the UK, with nearly 60,000 new cases diagnosed each year, according to Cancer UK.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Approximately 15 to 20% of breast cancer cases are HER2-positive, meaning the breast cancer cells have higher than normal levels of a protein called HER2 on their surface.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: In about 10% of cases, this treatment causes problems with heart function.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Survivors are currently advised to stay on these drugs for life, even after their cancer treatment ends and their heart recovers.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Dr Sonya Babu-Narayan, clinical director at the British Heart Foundation and consultant cardiologist, said: "These findings will be hugely encouraging for the thousands of breast cancer survivors whose heart health has been affected by lifesaving cancer treatment.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: "The study results give hope that many women will be able to safely stop medicines once their heart has recovered." Do you have a story suggestion for Beds, Herts or Bucks?

sentences.text: Friends Amelia (left) and Beatrice (right) are living at home when they start university this September More new students are choosing to live at home for university this year than in the last nine years, new data shows.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Over 81,000 UK 18-year-olds said in their accepted university application that they intended to live at home this year, according to the Universities and Colleges Admissions Service (Ucas) - just over one in three students in that category.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: In 2017, it was closer to one in five.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: The figures vary across the UK - with 48% of applicants in Scotland intending to live at home, compared with 20% in Wales - but the trend is rising across the board.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Students told the BBC the rising cost of living was a major influence in deciding what to do after school or college.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: For friends Beatrice and Amelia, who are from St Helens, Merseyside, the cost of accommodation was a big factor in their decision to live at home while studying.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Both are heading to university in September, but neither will be moving into student accommodation.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Beatrice is going to the University of Manchester to study maths and plans to commute by train, a journey which can take about 50 minutes in total.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "My first choice was Manchester and then my second was Liverpool, so I knew I could commute," she says, adding that the price of accommodation would have been "a few grand a year".
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Amelia, who is going to study at Liverpool John Moores University - approximately 20 minutes away by train - says the accommodation she found was between £300 and £400 a week.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Although neither is looking forward to the commute, both are still hoping they can get the full experience of university while living at home.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: My three-hour university commute is worth the £7,000 saving on halls However, fellow student Jessica, who is also going to study at Liverpool John Moores University, feels she will miss out.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: She says she would have loved to live on campus and enjoy student life, but the price of renting is "ridiculous" and "insane".
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "I have a part-time job as everything is so expensive, and then commuting is going to kill a lot of my free time as well," she says.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "It is a bit sad really when you think about it." But she is pleased that staying at home means she will still be able to have her mum and dad's cooked dinners.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Earlier this year, BBC News followed the daily journey of one first-year student who said she was saving over £7,000 on accommodation by commuting 90 minutes into Manchester each day from home.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: The figures were recorded on results day and are expected to rise over the coming month as more students accept university places through clearing.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: A record number of UK 18-year-olds have been accepted into university this year.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: But student rents have risen sharply in recent years, alongside other living costs.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: The Higher Education Policy Institute (Hepi) said last year that students needed £61,000 over the course of a three-year degree in order to have a "minimum socially acceptable standard of living" - and that's excluding tuition fees.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Its report found that in 2024 the cost of renting in university-owned accommodation ranged from £108 per week, for 40 to 44-week contracts in Northern Ireland, to £338 a week for the shortest contracts in London, where rent makes up nearly half (46%) of students' costs.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: In most areas it was between £140 and £180 a week, with private halls usually being more expensive.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Many students are eligible for a maintenance loan, which can help with the cost of accommodation, but the average annual price of a room on campus is increasing much faster, according to some student unions .
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Hepi says most young full-time students now work in paid employment during term time to make up the difference between their maintenance loan income and the cost of living.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: For some students, it means a rethink about what university looks like.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: The Open University, which offers distance learning and online courses, says more teenagers than ever are starting courses with it.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Almost 3,400 18-and 19-year-olds joined the university last year – making up 9.5% of new starters, compared with 5.7% six years ago.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Traditionally, it has been popular with mature students wanting to continue working while studying from home.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Its vice-chancellor, Prof Dave Phoenix, says it points to a shift in how younger people are thinking about university, adding that studying online "means they can avoid moving costs and high accommodation bills and, for others, it means keeping a job".
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: But a recent report , external by Prof William Whyte, from the University of Oxford, argues that the value of on-campus life extends far beyond the price of accommodation, and plays an important role in personal development and the wider university experience.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "The question isn't simply where students live.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: It's what they gain from living and learning together as part of a university community," he says.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "Currently, we have no real policy on accommodation for the overwhelming majority of students who want to leave home for study.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: It's time for a serious debate about the role accommodation plays in the university – and how we will pay for it." A spokesperson for the Department for Education says the government recognises that too many students are facing financial hardship.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: They say they are increasing maximum maintenance loans and reintroducing maintenance grants to help with living costs, as well as working with universities and councils to improve access to student housing.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: The Lib Dems say schools are approaching an "existential crisis" in teacher retention Burnt out teachers urgently need better working hours and more support to stop them leaving the profession, the Liberal Democrats say, as the new term approaches.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Nearly half of the teachers surveyed by the party in England said they were planning to quit the classroom in the next five years, with many saying they felt overworked and stressed.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The Lib Dems are urging new Education Secretary Lucy Powell to fully fund teachers' pay, rather than raiding school budgets to cover increases, and to bring in limits on overtime.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The Department for Education said last year saw the lowest rate of teachers leaving the profession since 2010 but acknowledged there was "more to do".
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The survey asked more than 900 teachers, headteachers and Special Educational Needs Coordinators (SENCOs) across England how long they planned to stay in teaching.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Almost half of those in post said they were considering leaving teaching in the next five years, while one in ten were planning to spend less than a year in the job.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: More than three quarters of those surveyed, which included former teachers, said they had felt "frequently or constantly burnt out" while at work.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Respondents cited high workloads on marking, lesson preparation and other tasks, which they said gave them less time in the classroom.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The Liberal Democrats' schools spokesperson Caroline Voaden said this pointed to a government that is "not listening" to the profession.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: "We rely on teachers to educate our children, the least we can do is make sure they want to come back after the summer," she said.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Teacher retention is a challenge successive governments have had to grapple with.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The National Education Union (NEU) reported that 4 in 10 teachers were planning to quit over "huge workloads and excessive accountability" in 2019.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: This latest survey was also conducted with the help of the NEU, as well as the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL).
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: "After over a decade of austerity and chronic underfunding in our schools the system is on its knees" said the NEU's general secretary Daniel Kebede.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: "The new academic year is the perfect time for Andy Burnham to signal a fresh start for our schools" he added.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The Lib Dem proposals include the government fully funding teacher's pay, which will increase in England by 3.5% from September, with an additional 3% the year after.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Currently, half of the pay increase will come from existing school budgets.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The party is also calling for proper enforcement of teacher's legally mandated working hours, the introduction of reasonable limits on overtime, and for all schools to be required to introduce flexible working policies.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The party did not identify where funding might come from to pay for the policies.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: An education department spokesperson said: "We know teachers do an incredible job and we're determined to make sure that dedication is matched with the right support.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: "Last year saw one of the lowest rates of teachers leaving the profession since 2010, and a record number of teachers returning to the classroom, but we know there's more to do.
