sentences.text: The BBC spoke to parents and experts to find out their back-to-school tips It's back-to-school time again - and families brace for the challenge of swapping summer lie-ins for school routines, easing first-day nerves and getting ready for the year ahead.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: While children in Scotland returned to school in mid-August, children in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will be returning in the coming week as September begins.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: We spoke to experts to find out their six key tips to make going back to school as stress-free as possible.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Cerys Parker, a teacher and blogger, says one of the best ways to keep organised during school time is to keep a consistent morning routine.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Her morning starts 30 minutes before her children wake up, for some alone time and a hot coffee.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She  then makes them the same breakfast every morning, which they eat together with no screens, then it's upstairs for showers and getting ready for school.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker also keeps copies of her children's timetables so she knows what to prepare on specific days, such as when they have PE She grabs their lunch boxes and they leave the house at 07:30 for the bus, or 07:50 if Parker is dropping them at school on the way to her own job.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The night before, she makes sure school bags are packed, shoes are ready, uniform is laid out and lunch is packed for the morning.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "We have things in the same place, so the bags are always in the same location, the keys, and that makes the morning smoother.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: There's no panic about where everything's going to be." It is easy to forget non-uniform days, sports days or study sessions.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker recommends having a family calendar pinned to your wall or your fridge - somewhere you can easily see it every day.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's an academic year calendar with a space for each of us, and then an events section, so as soon as a notice comes in, I write it down." This could include things like meal plans, after-school activities or - depending on your child's age - exams.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: After school, many children are tired and are not up for discussion about their day, so Will Shield, professor of child and educational psychology at the University of Exeter, suggests changing your approach to the conversation.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask some open questions, instead of interrogating them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask what made you smile today?
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Or who did you play with at lunchtime?" These sorts of questions are a lot easier to answer for a child, he says, instead of asking what they did.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "See it as part of the process of separating and loving you, missing you, which is really important." Many families will have children attending school for the first time, which can be just as big a moment for parents as it is for new pupils.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Shield says parents should "reassure themselves" about the routine they will need to follow on school mornings.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Visit the school, walk or drive past it, bring bedtimes back a bit earlier so it's not just a big start in the first week," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's about much more basic things, like feeling comfortable and safe to be in a classroom with other children," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Building independence can also help bridge the gap between home and school life, she says, by encouraging your child to do some things by themselves, such as zipping up their own coat.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's just building that sense of, I'm ready to do this without you," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: But Deiros Collado also stresses that your child should be able to ask for help when they need it.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "One of the best skills you can give your little ones is being able to say to an adult, 'Help me,' because you want your kid to be able to say that to a teacher." She also suggests a "goodbye ritual" with your child to practise separation, such as blowing a kiss.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Katharine Radice says that focusing too much on the homework outcome you want for your child can be "demotivating" for them Katharine Radice, teacher and author, recommends putting together a homework timetable.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Doing this puts boundaries around homework and makes it easier to ring-fence distraction-free time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: This could be different every week depending on different activities, but Radice stresses there should be a plan in advance so it's not left to the last minute.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: For supporting children with homework, Radice suggests approaching the task in a "positive and open way" and listening to what they might be finding difficult.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She also recommends looking for opportunities to praise your child's effort in doing work to help them "stay motivated." "If your child thinks their outcomes won't meet your expectations, they may start to feel that their effort is pointless," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Some children who are returning to school may have anxieties about the year ahead, and Shield recommends to sit with your child and listen to their concerns.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Don't immediately reassure them by saying, 'You'll be fine,'" he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "The child's got no evidence they will be fine because they're worried." He suggests phrases such as "I can see you're worried" to make a child feel listened to.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: It is also worth trying to dig deeper to find out what is making them worried about school specifically.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: He also recommends some gentle encouragement of positive things they like about school to ease some worries, such as lunchtime or playing sports with friends.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: If anxiety does become overwhelming for them, if they aren't sleeping or it is stopping them from doing everyday things, then Shield recommends talking to the school or a local GP.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Dorothea Bate, born in 1878, had little formal education but a fascination with wildlife and nature A pioneering fossil hunter who was one of the first women to be employed by the Natural History Museum has been recognised with a national blue plaque.

sentences.text: Bate was born in Carmarthen, Wales, in 1878 and developed a fascination with the natural world from an early age.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: She moved with her family to rural Gloucestershire as a young woman and spent hours exploring the surrounding countryside and caves, collecting fossils.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: She had little formal education, instead largely teaching herself, and in 1900 asked for work behind the scenes at the Natural History Museum in London.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: Her determination impressed museum staff, earning her a position as an assistant and beginning an association with the institution that would last more than 50 years.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: She published her first scientific paper, A Short Account Of A Bone Cave In The Carboniferous Limestone Of The Wye Valley, in 1901.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: Bate went on to undertake expeditions across the Mediterranean, often travelling alone to remote caves in search of evidence of ancient life.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: She achieved more than 80 published scientific papers, despite spending most of her career without a permanent paid position.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: In 2017, a blue plaque was dedicated to Bate at Napier House in Carmarthen where she was born.
sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: "She used this drive to make sense of ancient life through fragments of bone, bringing it to life once again," they said.

sentences.article_title: Pioneering fossil hunter recognised with blue plaque

sentences.text: Lee Fraser is the park ranger for The Mere Volunteers in a north Shropshire town have been able to litter pick inside a prominent lake because its water levels have dropped due to the recent hot weather.
sentences.article_title: Hot summer helps group clear 'buckets' of lake litter

sentences.text: With this summer being the hottest and one of the driest on record, lakes and rivers across the country have been running low.
sentences.article_title: Hot summer helps group clear 'buckets' of lake litter

sentences.text: It has meant Ellesmere park ranger, Lee Fraser, has been able to go into the Mere with volunteers and pick out litter, such as bricks, pottery and mobile phones.
sentences.article_title: Hot summer helps group clear 'buckets' of lake litter

sentences.text: He said the team have already collected "five big bucket loads" of litter which he said "covered half the distance" of the town's promenade.
sentences.article_title: Hot summer helps group clear 'buckets' of lake litter

sentences.text: Fraser said this year they decided to collect litter by standing in the water, as it was easier to see what was in the water.
sentences.article_title: Hot summer helps group clear 'buckets' of lake litter

sentences.text: "We tried it last year from a boat, which when you stand on the bank, you can see all the bricks.
sentences.article_title: Hot summer helps group clear 'buckets' of lake litter

sentences.text: "Once in the water, on the boat, even if you are next to them and someone's shouting that it's right next to you, you cannot find it.
sentences.article_title: Hot summer helps group clear 'buckets' of lake litter

sentences.text: "There are quite a lot of bricks out on the side now already and we have only been at it less than an hour", he said.
sentences.article_title: Hot summer helps group clear 'buckets' of lake litter

sentences.article_title: Hot summer helps group clear 'buckets' of lake litter

sentences.article_title: Hot summer helps group clear 'buckets' of lake litter

sentences.text: Candidates standing in the Isle of Man's general election have been sent letters asking them to back the island signing up to an international space treaty.
sentences.article_title: Manx space group urges election candidates to back treaty

sentences.text: The Manx chapter of the Mars Society wants the island to become a signatory to the Artemis Accords, the framework for peaceful, transparent space exploration now backed by more than 70 nations, including the UK as a founding member.
sentences.article_title: Manx space group urges election candidates to back treaty

sentences.text: The accords, launched by Nasa in 2020, are non-binding and require no parliamentary ratification, membership fee or financial contribution to sign.
sentences.article_title: Manx space group urges election candidates to back treaty

sentences.text: Chapter leader Stuart Mullan said it was a "low-risk, high-visibility way" for the island to show ambition around space projects.
sentences.article_title: Manx space group urges election candidates to back treaty

sentences.text: "Signing the Artemis Accords costs nothing and commits us to nothing beyond principles we already stand for," said Mullan.
sentences.article_title: Manx space group urges election candidates to back treaty

sentences.text: "Joining the accords would put us on the map internationally and gives a real boost to the case for developing more STEM [science, technology, engineering, and mathematics] projects on the island." The Isle of Man's Space Registry handles satellite filings for some major space operators.
sentences.article_title: Manx space group urges election candidates to back treaty

sentences.text: "Nobody is suggesting the Isle of Man starts launching rockets," Mullan continued.
sentences.article_title: Manx space group urges election candidates to back treaty

sentences.text: "All we ask is that candidates consider promoting the Isle of Man as an attractive base for STEM companies and businesses, the kind that bring skilled, well-paid jobs the Island badly needs right now.
sentences.article_title: Manx space group urges election candidates to back treaty

sentences.text: "The space sector globally needs the same things the Island already provides for aircraft and shipping.
sentences.article_title: Manx space group urges election candidates to back treaty

sentences.text: "Finance, legal services, tax expertise, insurance, and regulatory know-how.
sentences.article_title: Manx space group urges election candidates to back treaty

sentences.text: It would be a strange decision not to look seriously at whether the Isle of Man can capture a share of an industry that's growing this fast.
sentences.article_title: Manx space group urges election candidates to back treaty

sentences.text: We think it can." Elon Musk's Space X company operates a satellite ground station on the island while satellite giants including SES, Inmarsat, Avanti and Telesat have all registered spacecraft through the Isle of Man's filing system.

sentences.text: As wildfires worsen across large parts of Indonesia, a noxious haze is choking the region A blanket of toxic haze is enveloping parts of Indonesia and spreading into Malaysia, Singapore and the Philippines, as weeks-long wildfires continue to burn.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Millions of people across large swathes of South East Asia have been exposed to the smog, which in some areas has fuelled "acutely unhealthy" pollution more than 15 times the World Health Organization's recommended level.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Many of the ongoing fires have been burning across Sumatra and Indonesian Borneo since mid-July – underpinned by a so-called Super El Niño that is exacerbating drought conditions.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Between July and August, Indonesia's Health Ministry recorded over 50,000 cases of respiratory infections linked to land and forest fires.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: More than 12,000 of those cases are of children under the age of five.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Rizma Nur Fatimah, a 19-year-old teaching assistant at a school in Banjarbaru, South Kalimantan, told the BBC that the smog in her classroom had become so thick "you couldn't even see your own feet".
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: "Even inside the house, with everything closed, the haze still got in," she said.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: "We've been living with this since I was born.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: It's the same every year, so we've almost become resigned to it.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: But this year is worse." Misbah, a 23-year-old mother from nearby Pengayuan village, said her three-year-old daughter had developed "a cough, a sore throat and a runny nose" during the haze.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Some 1,300 kilometres away, in the Philippine island province of Palawan, residents reported similar symptoms, including itchy eyes, nose and throat.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: "We are now experiencing mild headaches," said Dr Precious Bañas-Melad.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: "My cousin who isn't allergic to anything started developing allergies.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: My husband is the first one who had itchy eyes and throat." Malaysia, meanwhile, has reported rising cases of asthma and conjunctivitis amid worsening air quality nationwide as smoke continues to drift across the border.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Indonesia's forest and peatland fires are not a new phenomenon.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Experts say the crisis is rooted in decades of land-use change, dating back to the Suharto era, when vast areas of rainforest and peatland in Kalimantan were opened for logging, plantations and large-scale development projects.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Today, large-scale fires are often associated with the expansion of industrial plantations and other commercial land use.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Environmental groups, researchers, and government investigations have repeatedly alleged that some companies use fire as a cheap and effective way to clear vast areas of land.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Some point out that while drought and El Niño conditions help fires spread, the severity of the haze is also linked to human activity.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Drained peatlands, industrial timber estates and oil palm plantations can leave landscapes more vulnerable to burning, with fires often recurring in the same areas.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Unlike traditional practices, which are small-scale, community-managed, and closely monitored, fires linked to large-scale land development can be far more difficult to control and can cause environmental and public health impacts on a much larger scale.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: What makes Indonesian Borneo's wildfires particularly worrying is that they are burning through one of the world's largest tropical peatland ecosystems.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Under normal conditions, these peatlands serve as gigantic carbon reservoirs.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: But under abnormal conditions, such as those currently hitting the region, they can become carbon "bombs".
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: "But this also means they can become a 'carbon bomb' when they are drained or burned, because that carbon can be rapidly released into the atmosphere." Others have warned that as the current Super El Niño continues to escalate over the coming months, the fires could significantly worsen.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Last year, without El Niño, forest fires in Indonesia torched a 359,000-hectare area, says Professor Bambang Hero Saharjo, a forest fire forensics expert from Institut Pertanian Bogor University.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Citing research reports, Prof Bambang told the BBC that this year's El Niño could burn an area as large as 11 million hectares – putting it on par with one of Indonesia's worst wildfire seasons, which happened from 1997 to 1998.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Earlier this week, Indonesia's forestry minister Raja Juli Antoni told reporters that the battle to extinguish the current wildfires was entering a critical phase.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: "Our problems are not over.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: September is the peak of El Niño," he said earlier this week.
sentences.article_title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies

sentences.text: Scientists may have found evidence of dark matter for the first time in an underground lab Scientists believe they may be one step closer to detecting dark matter for the first time, but the findings have not been verified by independent researchers.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Scientists from the University of Bristol were part of a two-year study to try and measure the invisible substance thought to make up over 85% of the universe.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Using a sensitive detector in an an underground laboratory in the US, the researchers saw an atom and mystery particle colliding.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Lead researcher physicist Dr Sam Eriksen said it could be "the first step in understanding dark matter as a particle", but further research could also reveal that the particle is not related to dark matter.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: "Following a huge amount of scientific effort, this is incredibly exciting," the University of Bristol senior research associate added.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Although scientists have long been certain of the existence of dark matter, because it is invisible as it reflects no light.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: While it is thought to make up the majority of mass in the universe, it has never been directly detected.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: It is managed by the US Department of Energy's Sanford Underground Research Facility in South Dakota - the deepest laboratory in the US at nearly a mile beneath the ground.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Scientists studied data from one of the world's most sensitive dark matter detectors To search for dark matter, LZ uses extremely sensitive light detectors to capture particle interactions.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: The study found one particle interaction which could potentially have been caused by a Weakly Interacting Massive Particle, (WIMP), which scientists believe make up dark matter.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: But there is currently low statistical evidence in it being a true breakthrough. 'I would be dead if I had not learnt about little-known law' How many times has Clare's Law been used in the West of England?
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: Crews still battling industrial fire after blasts heard The findings were revealed at a conference in Japan on Tuesday, but the research has yet to undergo peer-review by other scientists.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: The findings have been rated 2.6 sigma, which is the system that marks the statistical significance of discoveries.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: The normal threshold is five.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: "With only one event, we don't want to get ahead of ourselves," said Professor Rick Gaitskell from Brown University.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: "We are not claiming to have seen dark matter.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: "To date none provide a convincing explanation," he said.
sentences.article_title: Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter

sentences.text: "It's an incredibly exciting time, the kind of event every astro-particle physicist dreams of, and we can't wait to analyse more data to see if additional candidate events appear." sentences.text: OpenAI's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki has called for "extreme caution" over AI's runaway progress and warned more intervention may be needed to ensure "humans remain in control of the future".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: "I am concerned no one is prepared for the consequences of a continued rapid rise in machine intelligence," he wrote in a blog post entitled "An Alien Mind , external ".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: The post comes only a few days after the ChatGPT-maker released its latest model GPT-6 Astra, which it called its most powerful product ever.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: OpenAI and other AI firms like Anthropic shared reports of their AI agents acting autonomously and carrying out real-world cyber-attacks on other companies.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: In July, OpenAI called an incident in which its AI agents - AI systems which can operate alone after human instruction - hacked the tech platform Hugging Face "unprecedented".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: Meanwhile in September a report claimed months earlier AI agents from the firm had also hijacked a German website.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: "We are facing a transition to a world with incredibly intelligent machines, and we need to ensure that transition works out well for humanity," Pachocki wrote in the latest blog post.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: He said OpenAI would continue to "build defensive systems" and seek technical solutions to alignment - a term used to describe ensuring a machine's actions and goals perfectly match human intent and safety guardrails.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: Pachocki added one of the firm's main priorities moving forward would be to build an "automated AI researcher" to keep pace with AI progress while ensuring ways that human researchers could remain part of the process.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: "Instead of better AI guardrails, regulations, or assurance to keep people safe, they propose developing internal AI agents to research these problems," said Professor Gina Neff, head of the Minderoo Centre for Technology and Democracy at the University of Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: "If Jakub and others at OpenAI want relevant folks in the AI industry to act in concert with them to make things go well, one of the most important things they can do is share far more information about what they are seeing that is making them call for caution," he wrote on X , external .
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: Global regulations are struggling to keep up with the pace of AI development.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: The European Union's AI Act came into force on 2 August, which requires AI giants like OpenAI to prove their most powerful models cannot autonomously launch cyber-attacks or evade human control before they are allowed to be sold in Europe.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: But because the law's jurisdiction is confined to Europe, it cannot stop a rogue AI developed elsewhere from threatening the continent.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: In his blog post, Pachocki called for legally or internationally required minimum safety thresholds which could be enforced by a "network of third-party auditors" or "government agencies".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: AI labs would need to meet these thresholds, he said, before they were allowed to continue scaling or deploy advanced models.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: He added he hoped "voluntary slow downs" - a self-imposed pause by companies in AI development - would become commonplace until shared guardrails were established.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: In August OpenAI said it had slowed down training some of its most advanced AI models to improve security.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI chief scientist warns no-one is prepared for consequences of AI

sentences.text: The report is from a group called Nightingale Collective and claims that in May OpenAI's agents started using DseWiki as their own message board, shared tips on how to avoid being detected and made 15,000 edits to it.

sentences.text: OpenAI said it could not "meaningfully respond" to Nightingale Collective's findings because it hadn't been allowed to review the report, which was first shared with news agency Reuters.

sentences.text: Fifa has been under pressure since a scrapped plan to sell stakes in its competitions to investment firms Legal action from the top European leagues and global players' union Fifpro against Fifa has been extended to include the world governing body's "abusive conduct" towards the women's game.
sentences.article_title: Legal action against Fifa to include women's schedule

sentences.text: European Leagues, which represents 53 professional divisions, including the Premier League, and 1,328 clubs in 34 countries, first filed the complaint to the European Commission to protect the welfare of men's players in October 2024.
sentences.article_title: Legal action against Fifa to include women's schedule

sentences.text: The complaint stated that Fifa abused a dominant position under European competition law allegedly by not including national leagues and player unions over the new men's international calendar announced in 2023.
sentences.article_title: Legal action against Fifa to include women's schedule

sentences.text: In a statement on Tuesday, it said it is extending the scope of its complaint to include "Fifa's abusive conduct regarding the women's international match calendar and related women's football regulatory decisions".
sentences.article_title: Legal action against Fifa to include women's schedule

sentences.text: "Fifa's conduct threatens the growth and financial sustainability of women's professional leagues, and risks player health and wellbeing," European Leagues said.
sentences.article_title: Legal action against Fifa to include women's schedule

sentences.text: "The European Commission must now act to ensure that EU law is respected and that the future of women's professional football is not determined unilaterally by Fifa.
sentences.article_title: Legal action against Fifa to include women's schedule

sentences.text: "The submission details the same pattern of conduct identified in the original complaint - Fifa holds conflicting roles as governing body and competition organiser, which gives rise to a conflict of interest.
sentences.article_title: Legal action against Fifa to include women's schedule

sentences.text: It also includes the Premier League, English Football League, Scottish Professional Football League, La Liga, Serie A and the Bundesliga.
sentences.article_title: Legal action against Fifa to include women's schedule

sentences.text: A Fifa spokesperson said: "Fifa believes in the power of dialogue as opposed to legal action and escalation, and our doors always remain open to reach agreements in the best interest of football.
sentences.article_title: Legal action against Fifa to include women's schedule

sentences.text: "As a matter of fact, a landmark agreement reached with Fifpro earlier this year enabled groundbreaking reforms to the global transfer system, jointly adopted in full consensus with all football stakeholders.
sentences.article_title: Legal action against Fifa to include women's schedule

sentences.text: Under England's selection policy, players can only be called up from overseas clubs in exceptional circumstances.

sentences.text: Baxter feels it is important the rules are not changed.

sentences.text: David Etor's first break came after designing and building a kind of "solar oven" in Nigeria A Nigerian man has shared the story of how he rose up out of "abject poverty" as a child, to become one of the leading UK academics in his field.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: David Etor, 43, who grew up in Nigeria, only learned to read and write aged 12 and was told as a child that "nothing good will come out of you", but is now a lecturer in the School of Electrical, Electronic and Mechanical Engineering at the University of Bristol.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: He told the BBC how his family was so poor growing up that his mum would pretend to cook food in a kitchen they shared with others, "to protect our dignity" in front of neighbours.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "I didn't see a way out," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: Speaking to John Darvall on BBC Radio Bristol about the publication of his memoir, Etor described growing up in a "compound" with several other families, all sharing a single kitchen, toilet and bathroom.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "It was a very poor neighbourhood.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: We were particularly very poor that the poor neighbours would refer to us as poor," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "I do remember that there was a time where my mum would boil water.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "[She would] go back in and out, lift the lid, stir the water, go back into the room [and] come back as though she was preparing food...
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "She would come back in with that pot of water after a couple of hours and it will be as though she's just finished cooking a meal, but it was just water.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: To solve the problem, he designed and built a kind of "solar oven".
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "It worked incredibly well," he said, which led to an award from the state government and a job.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: That subsequently led him to receive a scholarship to study electrical power at Newcastle University and a PhD at Durham University, before he secured his current job in Bristol.

sentences.text: The Mercator projection is the map widely used across the globe but inaccurately depicts the sizes of countries and continents The UN has just called for the predominant world map to be replaced with one that more accurately reflects the true size of continents such as Africa.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The "Correct the Map" resolution adopted by the General Assembly aims to fix the discrepancy with the Mercator map, in which the African continent is shown as being of similar size to Greenland - even though it is in reality about 14 times larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN adopted a new map, the Equal Earth projection, which better represents the true sizes of landmasses - but comes with problems of its own.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: There have been many prominent attempts over the years to solve the problem of accurately representing the surface of a sphere on a flat rectangle, each with its own benefits and drawbacks.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Mercator projection has been around since the 16th Century and was vital for navigating the oceans The now widely used Mercator map was created in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Its main purpose was to help European sailors navigate the oceans, as cartography Professor James Cheshire at University College London explained.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "He wanted a straight line to be drawn on a map to look like a straight line in reality if you followed a compass bearing," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "That was what it was intended to do, and that's what it does brilliantly well." To keep those angles correct on a flat map, Mercator had to stretch the grid lines wider as they moved away from the equator toward the poles.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: His map accommodates for the curvature of the Earth by making countries near the equator seem much smaller than they are and countries nearer the poles appear stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The distortion is a result of it being impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: More than 450 years on, Mercator's creation is still the basis for many of the maps we see in classrooms, on TV and online, including Google Maps.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But critics of the Mercator map say there is a psychological effect to viewing some places as smaller than they actually are and others as larger, as we instinctively view bigger things as more important.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: For Kenyan geographer Kioko Muendo, this has implicitly downplayed Africa's vast resources, population and investment opportunities.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "Maps are more than just guides for travellers - they shape how regions are perceived politically and economically," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Equal Earth map aims to represent landmasses' area more fairly The Equal Earth map aims to address this problem with the Mercator projection.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It was developed by a team of cartographers in 2018 to present the size and shape of landmasses more accurately, and was inspired by the 1963 Robinson projection - a map that shows the entire globe's surface at once.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: As a result, the Equal Earth map was adopted by African Union members in February, before it was adopted by the UN.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But it sacrifices the straight lines that made the Mercator projection perfect for navigating with - and it cannot be used for measuring the true distance between different places.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "You can preserve area, or you can preserve shape, or you can preserve distance and direction, but not everything at once perfectly, because otherwise you'd be back to a sphere," Cheshire said.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Peters map projection gives a fairer idea of land area but distorts shape The Peters world map was designed by German historian Arno Peters in the early 1970s.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The rectangular map is based on the projection first described by Scottish cartographer James Gall in 1855.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The projection sacrifices accuracy of shape in favour of accuracy of scale.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: So, polar regions are squished, while the bits near the equator are stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This fixes the Greenland-Africa size issue, allowing those who use it to get a sense of the comparative size of different landmasses, all while preserving straight lines of longitude and latitude.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: However, the map severely distorts the shapes of Earth's landmasses, making them all look slightly off.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Russia, for instance, looks much smaller than it actually is.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The straight lines on the Peters map also do not represent true constant compass bearings and so are useless for navigation.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This Mercator projection puts the Americas front and centre instead of Europe and Africa In the same way the apparent size of a landmass can influence its perceived importance, so can its prominence on a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Some cartographers have attempted to orient the map so the south is at the top, to counter the psychological bias that comes from the global south being viewed as less imporant because it's lower down.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: And depending on where you are in the world, which continent is placed in the centre of a map can vary.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: While these alternate maps offer a different perspective on the world to the one we may be familiar with, they don't solve the issue of prominence, but rather simply change the focus of a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN flag is centred on the North Pole so no one continent is the primary focus One way of resolving the issue of which landmass is at the centre of a map - and therefore the most prominent - is putting none of them at the centre.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This is what the map in the UN logo does: the world is centred around the North Pole, with the continents radiating outward from it.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It's known as an "Azimuthal equidistant projection", placing world regions on a circular map around a focal point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The further away from that point on the globe, the bigger the circle.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On this type of map, all points are at the correct "azimuth" - or horizontal direction - from the centre point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But to fit the entire surface of a sphere onto a circle, the map becomes more distorted the further away from the centre it gets.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On the UN map, for instance, areas near the South Pole appear squished and stretched as what would be a ring of the same circumference as one around the North Pole becomes much larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Abraham Mofokeng was 20 when he joined a peaceful protest in Sharpeville Abraham Mofokeng still carries the wounds of the bloody suppression of a protest in South Africa 66 years ago.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: In what became known as the Sharpeville massacre, police infamously opened fire on thousands of peaceful demonstrators.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: A bullet is still lodged in Mofokeng's spine, and he has a gentle limp from a gunshot to the leg.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: "We weren't seen as people," the 86-year-old tells the BBC as he explains the reasons he joined the demonstration on 21 March 1960 against the repressive laws of the white-minority government.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: "All you were good for was working.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: You couldn't question them, you were supposed to just do as you're told." The massacre at Sharpeville, which he survived, exposed to the world the violence of the racist apartheid system - yet thanks to an indemnity law passed a year after the killings, none of the perpetrators were ever prosecuted.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: Mofokeng is now part of a legal case announced on Thursday that will seek to overturn this law.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: At least 69 protesters were shot dead by police on that day in 1960, becoming a pivotal event in the history of the anti-apartheid movement.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: Though Sharpeville may be a place name rich in historical resonance, it scarcely looks like a site that symbolises the struggle: the township is slowly crumbling.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: The once tarred roads of this area south of Johannesburg are returning to dirt.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: Many of the houses are still the small, brown-faced brick homes built under the apartheid-era government.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: The earth is dry and barren - heaps of rubbish are piling up throughout the neighbourhood.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: While the legalised system of racism was buried in 1994 when the country held its first democratic election and elected Nelson Mandela as president, its scars remain.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: There have been attempts at redress - not least through the Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) - set up by Mandela's government to investigate crimes committed during the apartheid era.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: But the Sharpeville survivors feel they have not seen justice.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: Protesters started fleeing as the police opened fire Sharpeville's local memorial park, the Human Rights Precinct, tells the story of how the streets of township became the scene of a bloodbath.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: Inside the park stand 69 white pillars, one for each life lost.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: The victims were killed while demonstrating against the racist pass laws.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: At the time, black people were forced to carry a document known as a passbook, known as "dompas" in Afrikaans, which restricted their freedom to move around the country.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: A person could be beaten and jailed if found without it - or if found in a "whites-only" area without permission.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: Many heeded the call from the leaders of the Pan Africanist Congress in March 1960 to march in protest against the dompas, including then-20-year-old Mofokeng.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: "The life we were living under apartheid was a life of oppression.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: We could not move around freely.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: "[The police] had rifles, machetes, even shields.
sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.article_title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa

sentences.text: The PDP's presidential candidate Olusegun Obasanjo swept to power in 1999, ushering in the  return to democracy Once the undisputed giant of Nigerian politics, the Peoples Democratic Party now finds itself on the brink of extinction.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: A question hanging over the campaign for January's general election, which officially kicked off this week, is whether the PDP can survive.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: A factional struggle that has ended up in the courts over who exactly is in charge could end up rendering it irrelevant at the ballot box.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: It is a remarkable fall for the party, founded in 1998, which appeared impregnable after the end of military rule a year later - so much so that its chairman boasted in 2008 that it would govern for six decades.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: For 16 years, it controlled the presidency - in the shape of Olusegun Obasanjo, Umaru Musa Yar'Adua and then Goodluck Jonathan - and the vast majority of the country's 36 states.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: But the 2015 federal election was a seismic shock.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: The PDP lost the presidential vote to Muhammadu Buhari and the newly formed All Progressives Congress (APC) - a coalition of opposition parties and disgruntled former members.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: Goodluck Jonathan (R) handed power over to Muhammadu Buhari (L) in 2015 after losing the election - a defeat that started the PDP's decline Thrust into the political wilderness the party's national leaders were bewildered - familiar with the trappings of federal power they had to work out what to do in opposition.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: This was the beginning of the end, according to political analyst Ishaq Buhari.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: "They were a party that was so used to power, being in opposition was a new challenge they struggled with from the start," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: If 2015 was a major blow, 2025 was the year the party's foundations were left in ruins.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: It was marked by a dizzying wave of defections and bitter internal conflicts.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: A group of state governors switched party allegiance, which had a particularly devastating effect.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: At the start of that year, the PDP still held eight states.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: But by December, five state governors - from Delta, Akwa Ibom, Enugu, Bayelsa and Rivers - had gone over to the ruling APC.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: They cited the PDP's declining viability and a desire for better co-operation with the federal government as reasons for their departure.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: Early this year, the PDP held three states but that is now down to zero - with the Oyo governorship slipping from the party's hands just last month.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: In 2019, these women supported Atiku Abubakar as the PDP candidate for president - he left the party in 2025 Internal power struggles, factionalism, insistence that power rotates through the regions and disciplinary measures have all added to the sense of disillusionment within the party.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: The PDP has been robbed of high-profile figures and talent, including the defection of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar last year.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: The crisis was intensified by a debilitating leadership tussle.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: In November 2025, a faction of the party, which observers say represented the majority of members, held a contentious national convention in Ibadan, Oyo state, despite court orders attempting to stop it.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: The convention expelled Nyesom Wike, a prominent PDP member who is serving in President Bola Tinubu's APC-led government.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: Wike, who helped found the party, heads a rival faction creating a political stand-off that has paralysed the PDP.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: He had controversially helped the APC win Rivers state in the last presidential election leading to accusations that he had betrayed the PDP.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: But in the eyes of the law the faction that he heads is the legitimate party.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: This means that it has been able to submit its slate of presidential and parliamentary candidates to the electoral commission leaving the rival faction without any representatives on the ballot.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: Those who think there is still hope for the party look to its historic supporter base Despite the chaos, some die-hard loyalists remain optimistic.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: Politician and staunch PDP member Aminu Adamu, part of the anti-Wike faction, believes a return to its former glory is possible.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: He cites examples from Thailand and Argentina, where parties have bounced back after years in the wilderness.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: "We have seen it happen before," he tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: "All we need to do is put our house in order and start to build from there.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: "If we make all the necessary corrections, by 2032 I really think PDP can be a major force again." Others point out that the party still has a grassroots network - essential to win and sustain power - with offices, activists, supporters and local leaders.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: But by 2032 it may be too late.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: With the party in such disarray and candidates backed by Wike on the ballot - voters are unlikely to trust them.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: Analyst Deji Olarenwaju believes the only thing that could save the once-mighty party is an alliance with the African Democratic Congress - now seen as the biggest opposition group or Peter Obi's Nigeria Democratic Congress.
sentences.article_title: Why Nigeria's one-time political giant may face extinction

sentences.text: "Because on their own they are going nowhere," he says.

sentences.article_title: The phone book that led us to Assad's spy chief in hiding
